correctness.rationale: The published per-gap floor formula is independently reduced to a fractional-part inequality. The proof separates the two offset half-periods by k parity, with correct weak and strict endpoints, identifies nested intervals of measure (1-epsilon*k)/(2-epsilon), derives exact survival probabilities and expectations, and bounds the parity-grid count uniformly within epsilon of its continuous cutoff. The triangular limit and 3epsilon CDF error then follow. 847 exact rational floor-iteration cases plus symbolic rational tail identities test the algebra, but the argument is analytic for all real admissible parameters.

value.rationale: Near the unit negative flip a finite family of coexisting 2-cycles proliferates at order 1/epsilon. The canonical affine offset is naturally defined modulo its conjugacy period, so exact parameter-space proportions quantify how prevalent large cycle multiplicity is, not an arbitrary arithmetic slice. The complete finite-epsilon tail and nondegenerate universal Uniform[0,1/2] law identify the sharp parameter-dependent bifurcation profile and quantify robustness under unknown offset calibration; neither follows simply from the fact that cycles exist. No paper-sized downstream contribution is asserted.
